advice_inventory_mapping.exact_prose:
The positive `--max-wait-ms` bound covers SQL, cleanup and reporting under
the same original deadline. Once it expires, no new SQL starts, even if the
store is free. Zero permits immediately available work within a fixed
one-second allowance, with no lock retries; it does not mean zero execution
time. Keep the one-second reply margin above. These bounds depend on the
host scheduling AD and on interruptible database and filesystem operations.

advice_inventory_mapping.exact_prose:
An `ErrInternal` reporting an unconfirmed commit is different from a
precommit refusal: the verdict may already be recorded. Inspect the durable
request with `get-permission` and its `request_token` before deciding whether
to retry. Do not infer that nothing was written, resend an uncertain approval,
or automatically replay the call. Cancellation does not undo an already
committed verdict. After a confirmed commit, later deadline exhaustion keeps
the verdict and returns the available delivery facts; follow `not_confirmed`
as above. A decision or delivery response is not a receipt that its audit
events have reached durable storage.
advice_inventory_mapping.literal_follow_scope: Create real uncertain COMMIT response through existing actual SQLite boundary, inspect the actual durable request using the existing public get-permission/GetPermission owner, and make no replay of the committed allow. Follow the retained not_confirmed polling sequence where relevant; delayed audit reporting must not undo verdict or become a durability claim. Existing standalone Store-level commit uncertainty plus invented serialized errors is not by itself literal execution of caller recovery.
